prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Produce ONE square production repair atlas of exactly NINE circular tokens in THREE columns and THREE rows. REFERENCE 1 is icons-02, a five-column four-row atlas; REFERENCE 2 is icons-04, also five columns and four rows. They are the existing token edit targets, not a source of extra subjects. Extract the specified subjects and preserve their composition, painted character, identifying silhouettes, scale and colors except for the explicit corrections below. Do not reproduce either complete reference sheet.

Match the established luminous opaque gouache and selective fine ink, textured deep lapis interiors, jade/turquoise water, burnt ochre and grey mineral land, warm ivory light and very narrow ivory-gold circular rims. Strong simple features must read at 64px. Each perfect circle is centered in its equal square cell, with diameter 80 percent of the cell width, opaque painted interior and transparent exterior. Use generous transparent gutters; no crop contamination, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines, captions, modern equipment or watermark. These are symbolic painted tokens, not shiny coins.

CRITICAL EARLY-WORLD CONTINUITY FOR EVERY CELL: above-water land is completely BARE MINERAL ROCK, GRAVEL OR SEDIMENT, ochre/grey rather than plant green. No green tufts, grass, moss, roots, bushes, trees or plant-like land texture. In the final two marine-ecosystem cells only, green kelp and algae remain visibly below the water surface; coral is underwater too. Do not copy the incorrect plants or early cave openings from the references. All depicted hooked cliffs remain SOLID AND UNBROKEN, with no cave, arch, hole or entrance. First rain falls onto COOL SOLID GREY STONE, with no glow, lava or fire. Preserve water and marine life where explicitly specified.

Exact row-major order and target edits:

CELL 1, TOP LEFT, Tidal shore, from REFERENCE 1 row 2 column 4. Close the existing arch completely with solid matching ochre-grey cliff rock. Retain the same hooked outer cliff profile, tidal pools, exposed shelf and sea. No cave mouth, tunnel, natural arch, dark opening or vegetation. Target subject: A shallow jade sea recedes from a solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey cliff, exposing a broad wet mineral shelf dotted with small tide pools. The cliff has no cave, arch or opening, and every exposed land surface is bare rock or sediment without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

CELL 2, TOP CENTRE, First rain, from REFERENCE 1 row 2 column 1. Replace every glowing orange crack and molten patch with cool solid grey stone. Retain the cloud, falling drops and readable splash; remove hot vent-like steam columns. Crack interiors are dark unlit stone, never orange lava. No fire or vegetation. Target subject: Large bright raindrops fall from a low grey-white cloud onto cool, solid grey stone, making pale splashes and small dark wet patches on its closed, unlit cracks. All land is bare mineral rock; there is no molten lava, fire, orange glow or vegetation.

CELL 3, TOP RIGHT, Rainfall, from REFERENCE 1 row 3 column 2. Remove every green or golden plant-like tuft from the hillside and stream bank, replacing it with naturally painted bare rock and mineral sediment. Preserve the cloud, slanting rain curtain, hills and water route. Target subject: A broad grey-jade cloud releases a visible curtain of slanting pale drops onto a bare ochre-grey mineral hillside and a small jade stream. Smooth rock slopes, loose sediment and rain-darkened stone carry no green tufts, grass, roots, moss or trees.

CELL 4, MIDDLE LEFT, Rivers, from REFERENCE 1 row 3 column 3. Replace all grassy or tufted banks and slopes with bare ochre-grey rock, gravel and sediment. Keep the river course and two merging tributaries readable, with no extra channel network. Target subject: One strong jade river winds from high grey hills across bare ochre mineral land, fed by two narrow tributaries that merge into its single channel. Exposed banks and hills consist entirely of rock, gravel and sediment, with no green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

CELL 5, MIDDLE CENTRE, Delta, from REFERENCE 1 row 3 column 5. Replace all vegetation and plant-textured bars with bare ochre-grey sediment, while preserving the triangular river-mouth fan and three outward distributary channels entering the sea. Target subject: A jade river splits into three outward-reaching channels across a triangular ochre sediment fan at the edge of a dark blue sea. Every bar, bank and upstream slope is bare ochre-grey mineral material, with no green tufts, grass, roots, marsh plants or trees.

CELL 6, MIDDLE RIGHT, Water cycle, from REFERENCE 1 row 4 column 2. Replace all green hillside vegetation with bare grey-ochre rock and sediment. Preserve the sunlit sea, mountain, cloud, river return and simple circular process strokes; no forest transpiration or greenery. Target subject: A compact island cross-section shows a sunlit sea, a cloud above a bare grey-ochre mountain and a jade river returning to the same sea, joined by one pale sweeping loop rising on the sea side and descending over land. Every above-water surface is exposed rock or sediment, without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.

CELL 7, BOTTOM LEFT, Trench, from REFERENCE 1 row 4 column 5. Rebuild the geological geometry instead of preserving the wrong giant chasm: ocean water remains a continuous upper band; the narrow surface trench sits at the plate contact. The LEFT oceanic slab curves down toward the right and continues unmistakably BENEATH the RIGHT slab, enclosed by solid mantle. Show that continuous descending slab in cutaway, not two vertical cliff faces bordering an open fissure; no abyss filled with empty water, fire or lava. Target subject: A side cutaway beneath a continuous blue ocean shows a narrow seafloor trough where the left rocky plate bends downward and continues diagonally beneath the neighboring right plate. Keep the descending slab visibly continuous below its neighbor within solid ochre-grey mantle, with only a narrow water-filled surface depression rather than a giant open fissure.

CELL 8, BOTTOM CENTRE, Coastal mosaic, from REFERENCE 2 row 3 column 3. Remove every green tuft and terrestrial plant from exposed headlands, replacing them with bare ochre-grey mineral rock. Preserve the spatially separate kelp cove and coral shallows, all visibly UNDERWATER, and their blue connecting sea. Keep the hooked cliff solid and unbroken, with no cave or arch. Target subject: An oblique strip of solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast contains separate cool dark kelp coves and warmer pale coral shallows, divided by bare rocky headlands and connected by blue water. All green kelp and algae remain visibly underwater; exposed land has no green tufts, grass, roots or trees, and the cliff has no cave or arch.

CELL 9, BOTTOM RIGHT, Living coast, from REFERENCE 2 row 3 column 4. Remove all green growth from dry cliff tops, exposed shelf and headlands. Preserve the kelp and algae only where visibly UNDERWATER, the separate submerged coral shallows and the strong sweeping tidal current. Exposed shelf is bare ochre-grey stone; hooked cliff is solid and unbroken, without cave or arch. Target subject: The solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast holds a submerged kelp cove, separate underwater coral shallows and a broad bare tidal shelf; one sweeping jade tidal current connects the habitats around the cape. Green life is confined to visibly underwater kelp and algae, while all exposed land remains mineral without green tufts, grass, roots, trees, cave or arch.

Final visual check within the delivered atlas: nine complete circles in this exact order; no plants on any land surface; no cave or arch in any cliff; first rain on cool solid grey stone; trench is a narrow subduction trough with a slab visibly bending underneath its neighbor. Keep the two late-coast habitats alive underwater and preserve the reference style.
